title: Money changer exec in Martin plunder case surrenders to NBI
summary: A co-accused of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has surrendered to authorities and was granted conditional immunity, according to the Office of the Ombudsman.

blocks.text: The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) released screenshots from CCTV footage showing former House speaker Martin Romualdez inside the detention facility.
MANILA, Philippines — A co-accused of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has surrendered to authorities and was granted conditional immunity, according to the Office of the Ombudsman.

The anti-graft body said Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Guevarra, who is facing a P7.4-billion plunder charge over supposed kickbacks from government projects, surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation after the prosecution moved to cancel his passport.

The ombudsman granted Guevarra conditional immunity, provided that he cooperates fully and truthfully in the case, turn over all of Samchan’s records and devices, remain in the country and stay under protection of the Department of Justice.
His immunity will be revoked and his prosecution will resume should he break any of the conditions, it said.
“Mr. Guevarra personally handled Samchan’s operations. His testimony and records will help the prosecution trace the movement of funds alleged in the charge sheet,” the ombudsman said in a statement.
It said Samchan has returned to the Bureau of Treasury all its earnings from the questioned transactions. However, the ombudsman emphasized that restitution does not erase criminal liability.
It is also not the basis of the immunity granted to Guevarra.

Meanwhile, a total of P855 million worth of projects, composed of pumping stations and street lights, are linked to detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) engineer Carlo Rivera told the Sandiganbayan.

During the bail petition of Estrada on his plunder charge, Rivera recalled in 2024 that former Bulacan First District engineer Henry Alcantara asked him about P355 million worth of projects that could be allotted to the senator.
It was then that he asked the DPWH section chief about available projects, and he was told the P355 million could be used for pumping stations.

Rivera said Alcantara gave him a separate project list for P500 million worth of solar street light projects for the third district in Bulacan, which he forwarded to then-DPWH National Capital Region director Gerard Opulencia upon the order of Alcantara.
